The coupled state is \(|l_1, l_2, l, m\rangle = |1, 1, 2, -1\rangle\). The total magnetic quantum number is \(m = -1\), which means any measurement of the \(z\)-components must satisfy \(m_1 + m_2 = -1\). The eigenvalues for \(L_{1z}\) and \(L_{2z}\) being \(-\hbar\) correspond to \(m_1 = -1\) and \(m_2 = -1\), which sum to \(-2\). Since this does not match the total \(m = -1\), the probability of this outcome is zero.

Answer: B
